At ZedgeHost, migration is free in every plan, so support can move the site for you. The steps below work for WordPress sites and plain HTML sites.

author: ZedgeHost Team

content.text: Most moves go wrong at one of two points: the site is copied while it is still changing, or DNS is switched before anyone has checked the copy. This order avoids both. Nothing below needs downtime, because visitors keep reaching the old server until the new one is proven to work.

items.text: Set up the new hosting account.
Order the plan that fits your site and add your domain to it. Do not cancel the old hosting yet.
Copy the files and the database.
A WordPress site needs both. Files alone will not run without the database, and the database alone has no theme or uploads.
Test the copy before you touch DNS.
Open the site on the new server with a preview link or a hosts file entry on your own computer. Click through pages, forms and the admin login.
Lower the DNS TTL a day ahead.
A short TTL means visitors move to the new server within minutes of the switch, instead of a day later.
Switch DNS, then wait.
Point the domain at the new server and keep the old host running for a few days, so stragglers and email still land somewhere safe.

blocks.text: Step 1: Set up the new hosting account first

content.text: Order hosting before you move anything. A single website fits the Starter plan at Rs 1,499 per year, which includes 1 website, 20 GB NVMe storage, free SSL, free cPanel, daily backups and free migration. Larger sites use the Standard plan at Rs 2,999 per year or the Business plan at Rs 3,999 per year. If your site has outgrown shared hosting, a VPS starts at Rs 1,699 per month. See

if you are unsure which one fits, and

for the plan details.

Add your domain to the new account as an existing domain. You do not need to buy a new domain to move hosts, and your domain registration does not change. If your domain is a .com, it still renews at Rs 3,999 per year with your registrar. For the full picture of what happens between ordering and activation, see
how ordering works

blocks.text: Step 2: Copy your files and database

content.text: A complete copy has two parts. In cPanel, the files live in public_html and the database is managed through phpMyAdmin. Download a full backup from the old host, or copy the files with File Manager and export the database from phpMyAdmin, then upload the files and import the database on the new server.

For WordPress, update the database details in wp-config.php to match the new database name, username and password you created on the new server. If the site address changes from http to https, that is handled by the free SSL on the new plan, so check the padlock after the move. See
how to start a WordPress blog in Pakistan
for how WordPress is installed and set up on ZedgeHost.

If you would rather not do this part yourself, use the free migration instead. Every ZedgeHost plan includes free website migration, so support moves the files and the database for you. You only need the login details of the old hosting account. Contact 24/7 support and they will confirm what they need before they start.

blocks.text: Step 3: Test the copy before you touch DNS

content.text: This step is what makes a zero-downtime move possible. Your computer has a hosts file that overrides DNS for your machine only, so you can browse your real domain on the new server while everyone else still reaches the old one. Add a line with the new server IP address and your domain, save the file, and open your site in the browser.

items.text: Open the homepage and five inner pages.
Look for missing images, broken styles and pages that load the old design.
Test every form.
Submit the contact form and any checkout or signup form, and confirm the email arrives.
Log in to the admin area.
For WordPress, log in at yourdomain.com/wp-admin on the new server and confirm posts, media and settings are all there.
Check the padlock.
Free SSL is included in every plan, so the site should load with https and show the padlock before you switch DNS.

content.text: Fix anything you find now, while the old site is still live for your visitors. A mistake found during testing costs minutes. The same mistake found after the DNS switch costs visitors.

blocks.text: Step 4: Lower the DNS TTL a day ahead

content.text: Every DNS record has a TTL, a time to live, which tells the internet how long to remember the old server address before asking again. Many records use 14400 seconds, which is 4 hours, or 86400 seconds, which is a full day. If the TTL is a full day when you switch, some visitors can keep reaching the old server for a day after the move.

A day or two before the move, change the TTL on the records you will change, usually the main A record and the www record, to 300 seconds, which is 5 minutes. Then wait at least the old TTL before you switch, so the short value has spread. When you finally change the record, the world follows within minutes. If you are also moving nameservers, note that nameserver changes can take longer to spread, so changing only the A record during the move is the smoother option.

blocks.text: Step 5: Switch DNS and watch the move

content.text: Point the domain at the new server. If your host gave you nameservers, update them at your domain registrar. If you manage DNS records yourself, change the A record and the www record to the new server IP address.

items.text: Check the site from your phone.
Your phone uses different DNS, so it shows the new server sooner than your computer sometimes does.
Check email the same day.
Send yourself a test email and confirm it arrives. See the email section below.
Keep the old host running.
Do not cancel the old hosting for at least a few days. Visitors with cached DNS and delayed email still need it, and it is your fallback if anything breaks.
Remove the hosts file entry.
Delete the line you added in step 3, so your computer stops forcing the new server and uses real DNS like everyone else.

content.text: Email is what people forget in a move. If your mailboxes live on the old host, create the same mailboxes on the new server before you switch DNS, with the same addresses and passwords. Then check that the MX records point to the new server, so new mail arrives there. Old messages do not move with the website files, so export or forward anything you need from the old mailboxes before you cancel the old hosting. If your email lives elsewhere, for example Google Workspace, leave the MX records alone and only move the website.

blocks.text: How much does it cost to move a website to a new host?

content.text: Moving itself costs nothing at ZedgeHost, because free migration is included in every plan. You only pay for the new hosting plan. A single website moves to the Starter plan at Rs 1,499 per year, and you pay in PKR with Easypaisa, JazzCash, Raast or bank transfer. See

blocks.text: 5 mistakes that cause downtime during a move

content.text: Cancelling first leaves you with no fallback and no live copy while the new one is still untested. Cancel only after the new site has run for a few days with no problems.

blocks.text: 2. Switching DNS before testing the copy

content.text: If the copy has a broken database connection or a missing file, every visitor sees the error the moment DNS switches. Test the copy on the new server first, with the hosts file, and fix problems while the old site is still serving visitors.

blocks.text: 3. Copying the files and forgetting the database

content.text: A WordPress site without its database shows an error page, even if every file copied perfectly. Always export and import the database, and update wp-config.php with the new database details.

If mailboxes are not recreated on the new server and the MX records are not checked, mail bounces or lands on the old server after it is cancelled. Recreate mailboxes before the DNS switch and test mail the same day.

blocks.text: 5. Moving at the worst possible time

content.text: Do not move during a sale, a launch or the busiest hour of your week. Move on a quiet day, when a small surprise costs you the least and support has time to help.

blocks.text: How long does a move take?

content.text: A small WordPress or HTML site can move in a day: an hour or two to copy and test, then the DNS switch, which follows within minutes once the TTL is short. Larger sites take longer to copy, and DNS can take longer to reach every visitor if the TTL was never lowered. The time that matters is the testing time, not the switch. If the copy is tested before DNS changes, the switch itself is quick. If you use the free migration, support handles the copy and tells you when the site is ready to test. See

for the plans a moved site usually starts on.
